chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū Ḥamzah, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, 'What is the right of the Imam upon the people?' He said: 'His right upon them is that they listen to him and obey him.' I said, 'Then what is their right upon him?' He said: 'That he distribute among them equally and act justly regarding the subjects. So when that is present among the people, he does not mind who takes here and there.'

key_terms.الرَّعِيَّةِ: the subjects or people under governance
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely designated leader whose authority is to be obeyed
key_terms.بِالسَّوِيَّةِ: with equality, without favoritism in distribution
key_terms.حَقُّ: a due right or binding claim
key_terms.يَسْمَعُوا: to listen attentively and accept what is commanded
key_terms.يَعْدِلَ: to act with justice and fairness
key_terms.يُطِيعُوا: to obey and comply with the Imam’s authority

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of the Imam over the people and the rights of the people over the Imam in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the mutual rights between the Imam and the people. The people must hear and obey the Imam, while the Imam must deal with them equally and govern with justice. It presents leadership in Islam as a relationship built on obedience to rightful authority and fairness toward the community.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Abu Hamza who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is the right of the Imam<sup>asws</sup> upon the people?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His<sup>asws</sup> right upon them is that they should listen to him<sup>asws</sup> and obey him<sup>asws</sup>’. I said, ‘So what is their right?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup>asws</sup> should distribute between them with the equality and do justice among the citizens. So when it was that among the people, so no one will fear who has taken this or that’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from abu Hamza who has said the following.

“I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.), ‘What are the rights of the Imam over the people?” He replied, “Of his rights over them is that they must listen to him and obey him.” I then asked, “What are their rights on him?” He replied, “Maintain among them equality and justice among the followers. When this prevails among the people then there would no fear as to who has taken this and that.”
